sections.html:
• Scientific name: Ameiurus platycephalus (Girard, 1859)
  • Common name: Flat Bullhead
  • Size: 290 mm (11.4") SL
  • Type locality: Savannah River drainage, near Anderson, South Carolina, U.S.A.
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2011)
North America: Atlantic Piedmont and Coastal Plain from the Roanoke River drainage in Virginia, USA to the Altamaha River drainage in Georgia, USA.
Occurs in mud-, sand-, or rock-bottomed pools of small to large rivers. Also found in lakes, impoundments and ponds.

• pH: 6.6 - 7.8
  • Temperature: 18.0-26.0°C (64.4-78.8°F)

Generally tolerant of water with low dissolved oxygen levels.
Open sand and rocks. Needs larger logs to hide under during the day.
A nocturnal feeder that feeds on mollusks, leeches, crayfish and tiny fishes.
Social with virtually anything they cannot swallow.
Females are much fuller bodied during the breeding season, which occurs in early spring.

Identification: flat head, relatively straight snout profile. Relatively short anal fin, rounded in outline, 21-24 rays. Large dark blotch at dorsal fin base. Gold yellow to dark brown above, dark mottling on side, dull cream below, dusky fins, narrow black edge on median fins; 11-13 rakers on 1st gill arch.

Etymology: Ameiurus means "curtailed", referring to the lack of a deep notch in the caudal fin. Platys means flat and cephalus, head.
Proceedings of the Academy of Natural Sciences of Philadelphia v. 11 (nos. 60-77), pp 161.
